### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **2** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/automation/:name/clone (route, bridged from symbol CloneFlowResponseSchema — its route source's handler names it))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/automation/:name/clone (route, bridged from symbol CloneFlowResponseSchema — its route source's handler names it))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-7.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/automation/:name/clone (route, bridged from symbol CloneFlowResponseSchema — its route source's handler names it))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **61** of **218** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **157** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **157**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **102** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **168** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7ba8b11f52215f945ef1fd417d38b1fb00d8c20e` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `019790643f1f1b0e503b71d2b007ac36b29ccc2d` — the merge of head `be18e3d1b06da2c7fbdadcb3c1382dd046c449ba` into base `7ba8b11f52215f945ef1fd417d38b1fb00d8c20e`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 019790643f1f1b0e503b71d2b007ac36b29ccc2d && git checkout 019790643f1f1b0e503b71d2b007ac36b29ccc2d
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 7ba8b11f52215f945ef1fd417d38b1fb00d8c20e be18e3d1b06da2c7fbdadcb3c1382dd046c449ba && git checkout -B drift-repro 7ba8b11f52215f945ef1fd417d38b1fb00d8c20e && git merge --no-ff be18e3d1b06da2c7fbdadcb3c1382dd046c449ba

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7ba8b11f52215f945ef1fd417d38b1fb00d8c20e
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 7ba8b11f52215f945ef1fd417d38b1fb00d8c20e` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `be18e3d1b06da2c7fbdadcb3c1382dd046c449ba`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/automation-api.zod.ts + packages/spec/src/api/contract.zod.ts (the `declaredCode` precedent the key name cites), packages/spec/src/automation/flow.zod.ts (`FlowSchema`, the `data.flow` member the pins' fixture must satisfy), packages/client/src/index.ts (`automation.clone`, first consumer of `CloneFlowResponse['data']`), packages/runtime/src/domains/automation.ts and packages/runtime/src/flow-clone.ts (the serving side and `FLOW_CLONE_NOTICE`), packages/runtime/src/route-ledger.ts (the clone row naming the schema), packages/runtime/src/domains/automation-flow-clone-custom-package.test.ts (parses the served answer through the schema), packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json (the shard the level axis reads), scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs and scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs (the gate that enforces the level rule), AGENTS.md §3 of the Human Minimum (the level rule). Read, not reviewed. Remainder of the diff (the changeset, the regenerated mdx, the test file) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept set of `CloneFlowResponseSchema.data` widens by one optional member `noticeCode: z.string().optional()`. Every answer that parsed on `main` (`{ flow, packageId, notice }`) still parses; an answer carrying a string `noticeCode` now parses where `main`'s `z.object` would have stripped it silently (the object is not `.strict()`, so on `main` the key was accepted-and-dropped, never refused). Widening, no narrowing. **Right.**
- `notice` stays `z.string()` required, its describe byte-identical to `main`. **Right.**
- Public type surface: `CloneFlowResponse` (`z.input`) and `CloneFlowResponseParsed` (`z.infer`) each gain `noticeCode?: string`. No export added or removed: `api-surface/api.json`, `declaration-map/api.json`, `export-origins/api.json`, `json-schema.manifest/api.json` unchanged on the head, and `check:api-surface` / `check:export-origins` / `check:declaration-map` are not owed a regeneration. **Right.**
- `authorable-surface/api.json` lists `api/CloneFlowResponse:data` and its three siblings on both `main` and the head, nothing below `data`; a nested key of a REST answer is not an authorable key, so the shard does not move and `Metadata-protocol: none` is a true reading of the tree. **Right.**
- `packages/client` `automation.clone()` returns `CloneFlowResponse['data']` imported as a type from `@objectstack/spec/api`; the return type gains the optional key with no source change in the client, and nothing in the client reads `data.notice` or `data.noticeCode`, so it type-checks against the widened shape by construction. No client changeset owed: the client publishes nothing it did not publish before. **Right.**
- `packages/runtime` clone handler answers `deps.success({ flow, packageId, notice: FLOW_CLONE_NOTICE })` with no `noticeCode`; the key is optional, so the served answer still parses, and `automation-flow-clone-custom-package.test.ts` (`CloneFlowResponseSchema.safeParse(answer.body).success === true`, `answer.data.notice === FLOW_CLONE_NOTICE`) stays green by construction. Serving the code is #29727's half. **Right.**
- `route-ledger.ts` clone row's note still spells `data` as `{ flow, packageId, notice }`. Stale by one optional key, prose only, and the PR body names it for #29727 to update when the server sends the code. Not a finding on this PR's `hits`; noted for #29727.
- Generated: only `content/docs/references/api/automation-api.mdx` moves (the `data` summary row and a new `noticeCode` nested-shape row). `check:generated` is answered by CI; see ② for the check-run state.

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/29758-clone-flow-notice-code.md`: `'@objectstack/spec': patch`, body carries `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none`; PR body carries the same two lines. **Patch is the level the repo's rules require; the triage audit's "spec minor" is superseded by ruling A and is not a finding against the PR.**

- AGENTS.md Human Minimum §3: "The level follows the kind alone: a kind takes at least **`minor`** on a package the diff moves, `none` takes **`patch`**; a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition." A key added to a served REST answer changes nothing a metadata author can write, so the kind is `none` and the level is `patch`.
- `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs`, "The LEVEL axis (#16055)", ruling A (maintainer, 2026-10-21, on #25105): "`none` grades every introduced entry `patch`"; "A non-protocol widening (REST) or narrowing (a driver, a posture) ships `patch`"; "`none` beside a `minor` is the half of the ruling with teeth ... refused whatever the package, moved or not". The `judgeLevel` branch `if (declared.protocol === 'none') { if (moved.length) none-baseline-moved; if (minors.length) none-minor; none-clean }` refuses a `minor` under `none` outright. The self-test pins the exact pairing this PR uses: `armVerdict('Clause-②: yes (widening)\nMetadata-protocol: none\n') === 'none-clean'` ("a `yes (widening)` with `none` beside it (a REST widening) ships `patch`").
- So the dev's deviation is the rule, not a workaround: a `minor` here would have been refused by `Check Changeset`, and correctly so. The gate is right; the triage line "a spec `minor`" restated the pre-ruling-A coupling of `Clause-②: yes` to `minor`.
- Consistency of the lines: `Clause-②: yes (widening)` names the accept-set widening ① confirms; `Metadata-protocol: none` names the unchanged authorable surface ① confirms; `patch` is what `none` grades. The two contradiction checks in the gate (`added` under `no`, `narrowed` without the `(narrowing)` arm) are not engaged. Consistent.
- Check-runs on the head at the time of this record: `Check Changeset` success (the level axis on this body and changeset is `none-clean`), `Governed Surface Queue Guard` success, `PR-body guards` success, `Check PR Size` success, `Spec property liveness` success, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates` success, `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests` success, `Check Documentation Links` success, `Dogfood Regression Gate` success; 7 skipped by design (opt-in and conditional jobs). Still in progress on two reads: Build Core, Build UI Deps, Build Docs, Test Core 1/8 through 8/8, Live E2E UI, Type Check · workspace / source gates / consumer gates / debt ledger, Lint · ESLint / docs & code guards / repo & tooling gates / CI, release & engine gates / scoped · query-options erasure / scoped · slot lookup & corpus. No failure on any completed run. The landing rule (landing-operations.md: all PR checks green, not the required subset) is still owed by those runs; this record does not stand in for them.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev flag (deviation): "Changeset is `@objectstack/spec` patch, not the minor the order named." Answered in ②: patch is required by AGENTS.md §3 and ruling A; no action.
- Dev flag (deviation): "No `@objectstack/client` entry." Answered in ①: the client's source does not move and its return type follows the spec type by import; no changeset owed.
- Dev flag (deviation): "The schema TSDoc also gained one sentence naming `noticeCode`." Read: the TSDoc sentence matches the describe (stable code, console shows its own translation, falls back to `notice` for an unknown or absent code). No action.
- `open_questions`: `[]`. None to answer.
- Author: PR `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, so no human login to name.
- Triage 6594892213 named "a spec `minor`" and "regenerated artifacts" as binding. The level point is resolved against the repo's written rule in ②; the regeneration point is met (the one artefact the member moves is regenerated, and the ledgers that did not move are shown in ① not to be owed). Escalation not needed: a seat does not out-rule AGENTS.md, and triage's line is the older coupling, not a maintainer ruling.
- Name veto window: `noticeCode` stays the seat's call. Precedent read in ④.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/api/automation-api.zod.ts` against card #29758's Wanted list, ADR-0126 §9 (no clone lineage, the notice is the stated fact), `declaredCode` in contract.zod.ts, and the first consumers (`packages/client` `automation.clone`, the runtime clone handler, #29706's Console mapping):

- **Optional, string, located beside `notice`.** `noticeCode: z.string().optional()` sits in `data` after `notice`; `notice: z.string()` is required and its describe is unchanged. An answer with no `noticeCode` parses; `notice` absent is refused with exactly one issue at `data.notice`; a non-string `noticeCode` is refused with exactly one issue at `data.noticeCode`. The pins' fixture flow (`name` matching `/^[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*$/`, `label`, `type: 'autolaunched'`, `status: 'obsolete'` which is in the `FlowSchema` status enum, two nodes, one edge) satisfies `FlowSchema`'s required members, so the "exactly one issue" assertions are sound against the live `FlowSchema`. Holds.
- **The describe tells a client what to do.** "a client maps a code it knows to its own translated sentence, and falls back to `notice` verbatim for a code it does not know or when this key is absent (an older server sends none). The values are the server's; `notice` stays the English fallback." That is the card's Wanted sentence, and it is the whole contract #29706 needs: map known, fall back otherwise, never drop `notice`. Holds.
- **No values enumerated.** The schema is `z.string()`, not an enum or literal; the describe names no code. The vocabulary stays with the server (#29727). This is the right side of the line: an enum here would make every new notice a spec release and would break the fallback story (an unknown code must parse, not be refused). Holds.
- **Regenerated mdx matches the describe.** The nested-shape row for `noticeCode` in `content/docs/references/api/automation-api.mdx` carries the describe text verbatim, typed `string`, marked optional; the `data` summary row reads `{ flow: object; packageId: string; notice: string; noticeCode?: string }`. Holds.
- **Key name against precedent.** `declaredCode` (contract.zod.ts) is the nearest: a `THING` + `Code` key, `z.string().optional()`, naming an open, producer-owned code beside a required sibling (`code` there, `notice` here). The other two `*Code` keys in `packages/spec/src/api` (`statusCode`, `authorizationCode` in documentation.zod.ts) are HTTP-shaped and not a closer fit. `noticeCode` reads as "the code of the notice beside it", which is what it is. Holds; the name stays under the veto window as the card says.
- **Attempt to break it.** (a) An empty string `''` parses as a `noticeCode`; the describe's "a code it does not know" covers it, so a client falls back to `notice`; `declaredCode` has the same latitude, and tightening to `.min(1)` here would diverge from that precedent for no consumer gain. Not a finding. (b) A server sending `noticeCode` without `notice` is refused, which is correct: the English fallback is the contract. (c) `main`'s schema silently stripped an unknown `noticeCode`; a server that ships the code before this spec lands would have had it dropped at a parsing client, which is why the contract-first order (#29758 then #29727) is right. (d) Transport: `CloneFlowResponse` is `z.input`, so a consumer typing an answer in hand may omit the key; `CloneFlowResponseParsed` is `z.infer`, where the key is `string | undefined`. Both are what an optional key should type to. No must-fix, no should-fix.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-30noxg`
Reviewed-by: `session_01JQwxbXsK9j25sd7eVwW96G`

**VERDICT: PASS**
